# KibaOS — full documentation for language models

KibaOS is a free, user-friendly Linux desktop developed by Kiba Labs, LLC. Its goal is to be as simple to use as possible. This document describes KibaOS, its architecture, its company, and its website in plain text.

## What KibaOS is

KibaOS pairs a hand-crafted desktop environment with a proven Linux foundation:

- Desktop environment: KibaDE, based on the Ash shell of ChromiumOS, built from the Lumen fork of Chromium.
- Base: Arch Linux.
- Browser: Chromium, included by default.
- Software installation: the Apps and Games store.
- File management: the Files app.
- Everyday tools: calculator, notes, and similar utilities.
- Updates: quiet background updates; the system stays current without an update center.
- Privacy: KibaOS does not collect or sell your data.
- Trial: KibaOS runs as a live system from an 8 GB (or larger) USB stick, so it can be tested without installing anything.
- First run: guided setup asks for language and accessibility preferences before the desktop appears.
- License: GNU General Public License v3. KibaOS is free and open-source software, free forever.
- Tagline: "Fast. Simple. Limitless."

## What Kiba Labs, LLC is

Kiba Labs, LLC is the company behind KibaOS. Its values: calm software by default, free and open source, privacy first, and software friendly to everyone. Contact: corporate@kibaos.com. The company's code is published at https://github.com/KibaLabsLLC and KibaOS downloads live at https://sourceforge.net/projects/kibaos/.

Team:
- Remi Collins Mixo (assumed name of Christopher Fox Junior) — CEO/Founder; leads R&D, HR, and PR; maintainer of KibaOS.
- Christopher Fricks — UI/UX design.
- Joseph Daniel — QA.
- Torter-RS — developer, known for Chamesle Linux at chamesle.org.

## Downloads and releases

KibaOS is distributed through SourceForge: https://sourceforge.net/projects/kibaos/. The "latest download" link always points at the current release; the files page lists every published version with its date and file details, including checksums and signatures where shown. Release notes accompany announcements on SourceForge. Source code is on GitHub at https://github.com/KibaLabsLLC/KibaOS. There is no version list on this website; the changelog page points at those authoritative records instead.

## Using KibaOS

Installing: download the image, write it to an 8 GB or larger USB stick, boot the computer from it, and follow the guided installer.

First run: guided setup asks for language and accessibility options; everything else works out of the box.

Everyday use: the KibaDE desktop provides the Chromium browser, the Apps and Games store, the Files app, and everyday tools. No terminal is required, though one is available.

Updates: the system updates quietly in the background and only asks for a restart when one is actually needed.

## Technical architecture

KibaOS runs KibaDE, a desktop environment based on the Ash shell of ChromiumOS, built from the Lumen fork of Chromium, on an Arch Linux base. The result is a desktop that behaves like a modern, simple operating environment while retaining the flexibility of Arch Linux underneath.

## Compatibility

KibaOS runs on most PCs. Because it is built on an Arch Linux base, hardware support is broad. The recommended way to test compatibility is the live USB: boot the system from a stick without touching the hard drive.

## Security

Vulnerabilities should be reported privately to corporate@kibaos.com, not in public issues. Machine-readable disclosure details are at https://kibaos.com/.well-known/security.txt. KibaOS keeps itself current with quiet background updates, and all source is public under the GPL v3 for review and audit.

## Accessibility

KibaOS asks for accessibility preferences during first-run setup, before the desktop appears. This website uses semantic HTML, a skip-to-content link, visible keyboard focus, respect for prefers-reduced-motion, text alternatives for meaningful images, readable contrast, and responsive reflow.
